items.followUp: Define an enzyme and state one way in which it speeds up a reaction.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of an inhibitor.
rubric.description: Defines inhibitors as substances that decrease or stop enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that inhibitors decrease or stop enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of an activator.
rubric.description: Defines activators as substances that increase enzyme activity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating that activators increase enzyme activity.

modelAnswer: Inhibitors are substances that decrease or stop the activity of an enzyme.
Activators are substances that increase the activity of an enzyme.

items.followUp: What are microvilli, and how do they help in absorption?

rubric.why: Tests the meaning and location of villi.
rubric.description: Defines villi as finger-like projections of the lining of the small intestine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing their finger-like shape and location in the small intestine.

rubric.description: States that villi increase the surface area for absorption of digested food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating their role in absorption or increasing surface area for absorption.

modelAnswer: Villi are numerous finger like projections of the lining of the small intestine.
They increase the surface area and help absorb digested nutrients into the blood and lymph.

items.followUp: Define endangered species and name three threatened animal species found in Pakistan.

rubric.description: Defines an extinct species as one with no living members remaining anywhere in the world.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that no living members remain or that the species no longer exists.

rubric.why: Tests the meaning of endangered species.
rubric.description: Explains that an endangered species faces a serious risk of extinction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing its risk of extinction.

rubric.why: Tests knowledge of threatened wildlife in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Names the Indus river dolphin as an example of threatened wildlife in Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the Indus river dolphin.

rubric.why: Tests knowledge of another threatened species found in Pakistan.
rubric.description: Names another appropriate threatened species found in Pakistan.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming one correct example other than the Indus river dolphin.

rubric.why: Tests understanding of a threat to endangered species or a conservation measure.
rubric.description: Gives a relevant cause of population decline or a suitable conservation measure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid threat or conservation measure.

modelAnswer: A species is extinct when no living members remain anywhere in the world.
An endangered species is one that is at serious risk of becoming extinct.
Threatened wildlife in Pakistan includes the Indus river dolphin, snow leopard, houbara bustard and green sea turtle.
Habitat destruction, hunting and pollution can reduce their populations.
Protecting habitats and preventing illegal hunting help conserve these species.
